text:
jo: quick FYI — proposing a minimal RBAC narrow for the build-scan service account that runs SAST/DAST in CI. this affects artifact access and KMS audit expectations. need security eyes before rollout.
priya: what's the absolute least privileges needed? can we avoid kms:decrypt from the scanner-sa entirely? :thinking_face:
jo: yes. plan: builder step creates ephemeral unwrapped artifact (signed URL or ephemeral blob) and scanner-sa only needs storage.objects.get on the ephemeral location and read metadata. no kms:decrypt on scanner-sa.
nathan: SAST has a medium finding in tools/packager.py where the packager exposes metadata fields that might look like key identifiers. scan id scans/3210. we need to treat them as sensitive in telemetry and ensure serializer redacts.
security-bot: SAST alert 'metadata-exposure' triggered in repo redwood/packager at tools/packager.py:124. See https://scans.internal/scans/3210. KMS audit logs retention policy: 90 days.
priya: rollout approach?
jo: staged rollout:
  1) dev canary: apply narrowed RBAC to scanner-sa in dev only. run scanner at reduced concurrency for 1h. collect audit logs.
  2) CI advisory window: make SAST advisory for 48 hours in main while we watch for missing symbols/errors and triage false-positives.
  3) enforce in prod after we confirm scanner can fetch ephemeral artifacts and SAST runs without systemic failures.

nathan: important: add a unit + e2e test that the packager redacts fields matching KEY_ID_[A-Z0-9]{6,} in metadata. attach test output to PR.

priya: how do we validate KMS audit to ensure scanner didn't call decrypt? paste a quick gcloud snippet to attach to the PR.
jo: use these queries post-canary:

# KMS decrypts by service account in last 60m
gcloud logging read "protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=\"scanner-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com\" AND protoPayload.methodName:\"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt\"" --limit 50 --project=redwood-dev

# Storage GETs by service account (ephemeral artifact)
gcloud logging read "protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=\"scanner-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com\" AND protoPayload.methodName:\"storage.objects.get\"" --limit 200 --project=redwood-dev

nathan: also add a DAST synthetic probe that injects poisoned metadata to the packager and asserts emitted events do not contain key-like patterns. attach DAST logs to PR.

devex: i'll update the PR template to require: RBAC diff, KMS audit query outputs, scanner smoke logs showing artifact fetch, unit/e2e redaction test output, and DAST probe logs if serializer changes. suppression requests must use the standard suppression form and link to tests.
oncall: rollback play if we detect leakage or unexpected kms.decrypt calls:
  - revoke narrowed binding immediately
  - pause the CI scanner runners
  - open INC-9000 and assign forensic owner
  - export last 2k scanner logs and artifacts to secure bucket
  owners: @priya (rollback exec), @jo (postmortem)

priya: we should also allow a temporary advisory mode for SAST where findings are labeled and triaged, not blocking, to avoid mass-merge failures while we tighten perms.

jo: agreed. will open PR #999 with RBAC diff + packager redaction patch. ETA canary in 3 hours, will paste audit and scanner logs here.
nathan: reminder on suppressions: only allow suppression if fix + tests are in same PR and security signs off. otherwise reject.

security-bot: Note: attach KMS audit export and the audit-smoke output to PR #999. KMS audit retention: 90 days.

jo: thanks all — follow-ups: devex updates templates, nathan adds tests and DAST probe, priya runs canary and monitors KMS logs, oncall readies INC-9000. will report back in this thread with outcomes. :lock:
